summary: A toggle for an on/off setting that takes effect immediately. It is a form control: it submits a value while on, resets with its form, is disabled by a disabled fieldset and validates required. It shows a label, an optional description and an optional error message, in two sizes.

checked.note: Whether the switch is on. Alias of the registered selected (the native name). The initial value is the default state and the one a form reset returns to.

name.note: The name the value is submitted under. Nothing is submitted without it.

value.note: The value submitted while the switch is on, as a checkbox does. Nothing is submitted while it is off.

disabled.note: Unavailable: cannot be focused or toggled, and is not submitted. A disabled fieldset ancestor has the same effect without changing this property.

required.note: The switch must be on for the form to be valid. While off, the form reports a missing value.

label.note: The visible text and the accessible name. A switch without a label warns, because a label for pointing at the host does not name the control.

description.note: A hint under the label, read with the control as its description.

errorMessage.note: Why the value is not accepted. Shown, and read with the control, only while validation is error.

validation.note: Whether the value is accepted. error shows the error look and marks the control invalid for assistive technology. Set by the author; required validity alone does not set it.

size.note: The size step of the track and thumb. The label text keeps its size.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.notes: The row holding the control and its text block.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The operable on/off element: the focus target and the one that carries the switch role.

anatomy.name: track
anatomy.notes: The pill that shows on or off through its fill.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: The circle that sits at the start when off and at the end when on.

anatomy.name: text
anatomy.notes: Stacks the label, description and error message beside the control. Absent when none of them is given.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: The visible label and the accessible name.

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: The error text under the description. Shown only while validation is error and a message is given.

label.notes: Given through the label prop, not a slot, so the accessible name and the label text cannot diverge.

change.note: Fired after the user toggles the switch, with the new value already on checked and in the form data. Not fired for a change of the checked property or a form reset.

focus-visible.trigger: The control has focus reached by keyboard.

disabled.trigger: disabled is true, or a disabled fieldset contains the switch.

accessibility.native: A native checkbox input with role switch, so the browser gives the checked state, Space activation and the required constraint.
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop. A label pointing at the host with for activates the control but does not name it.

formAssociation.note: Form-associated. Submits value under name only while on. form.reset() returns it to its initial checked state. A disabled fieldset disables it and re-enabling restores it, without touching the author's disabled. required makes an off switch report a missing value, and the native control gives the message and takes focus on reportValidity(). A label pointing at the host with for toggles it.

accessibility.targetSize: At least 24 by 24 CSS pixels for the operable area in both sizes (WCAG 2.5.8). The text block is part of the click target.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: A ring drawn outside the track for keyboard focus, at least 3:1 against the surrounding background.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Logs one console warning when no label is given.

keyboard.Tab: Moves focus to the switch, and away from it. A disabled switch is skipped.
keyboard.Shift+Tab: Moves focus to the previous focusable element.
keyboard.Space: Toggles the switch between on and off.
keyboard.Enter: Does not toggle. Submits the form the switch belongs to, as a native checkbox does.

aria: role=switch with its on state exposed as checked, from the native control.
aria-describedby points at the description text, and at the error text while it is shown.
No aria-required: the switch role does not support it, so required is the native attribute and is not announced as a role property.
The track and thumb are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
announcements: Label, role switch, on or off.
The description is read after the name; the error message is read with it while shown.
Toggling announces the new on or off state.

useCases.when: A setting turns on or off and the change applies as soon as it is toggled (notifications, dark mode, airplane mode).
useCases.use: Switch, with a label naming the setting.

useCases.when: The setting needs context, such as what turning it on does.
A switch must be on to continue (accept a mode, enable a prerequisite) and the form checks it.
useCases.use: Switch with required, and validation error with errorMessage once the author finds it unaccepted.

useCases.when: Switches sit in a dense settings list or a toolbar.

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch for a choice that is submitted with a form button, such as agreeing to terms.
antiPatterns.why: A switch signals an immediate effect; a choice confirmed later reads as a checkbox, and a screen reader user expects the effect of a switch at once.

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch with no label, relying on surrounding text.
antiPatterns.why: The surrounding text does not name the control, so a screen reader announces an unnamed switch.
antiPatterns.alternative: Always pass label; use it as the name of the setting.

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing one of several mutually exclusive options with a row of switches.
antiPatterns.why: Switches are independent on/off settings and do not exclude each other.
antiPatterns.alternative: Radio group, or Toggle Group for a segmented choice.

openQuestions.question: Should required validity alone (an off required switch after a submit attempt or reportValidity()) show the error look and the browser message, or only validation=error set by the author?
openQuestions.recommendation: Only validation=error set by the author. Keeps one source for the error look across all controls and avoids a second message that can disagree with errorMessage; the native message is still exposed through validationMessage and reportValidity().
openQuestions.answer: Recommended answer chosen: the error look and errorMessage follow validation only. Revisit when a shared field-level validation pattern exists.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch?
openQuestions.recommendation: No. The APG makes Enter optional for a switch; a native checkbox submits the form on Enter, and a form-associated control behaves like input.
openQuestions.answer: Recommended answer chosen: Space toggles, Enter submits the form.

openQuestions.question: Is the on state's prop spelled selected (the registered name) or checked?
openQuestions.recommendation: checked, which the API vocabulary already registers as an alias of selected. It is the native name and the one form-associated controls and FormData documentation use.

openQuestions.question: Does the switch offer hideLabel, a read-only mode, an indeterminate state or a label position (start or end)?
openQuestions.recommendation: No. None was requested; a switch has no mixed state, and the label sits after the control. Add one when a use case appears.

openQuestions.question: Do hover and pressed looks (a hover fill, a widening thumb while pressed) belong to the first version?
openQuestions.recommendation: No. Neither was requested and the pointer keeps the rest look. Add them with their tokens when the design asks.

openQuestions.question: A manual screen-reader pass (VoiceOver and NVDA) is needed to confirm the description and error are read with the switch.
openQuestions.recommendation: Run it before the status moves from beta to stable; the axe checks in the behavior spec cannot confirm announcements.
